To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
2-NP inhalation caused an increase of GSH and GSH-related enzymes while 1-NP inhalation increased GSH peroxidases.

short-term inhalation of 1-NP at a concentration of 100 ppm induced liver cytochrome P-450 and GSH peroxidise while 2-Np at the same concentration increased the levels of cytochrome P 450, GSH, GSH S-transferases, and UDP-glucose transferase.
inhalation exposure to nitropropanes induces alterations in hepatic enzymes that are involved in detoxification of reactive metabolites and in lipid peroxidation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of inhalation of vapors of 2-N-P and 1-NP at 100 ppm for four consecutive days.
the biochemical effects of 1-NP in rats after short-term inhalation exposures at air concentrations of up to 100 ppm.
the effects of short-term exposure to 1- and 2-NP on liver enzymes in the rat.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
2-NP was more potent than 1-NP in altering the hepatic enzyme activities in rats exposed by inhalation for 7 hours/day for 4 days at 100 ppm.

exposure of rats to vapors of either of the isomers at 100 ppm for a 4-day period does not produce any significant alterations in the activities of liver enzymes involved in xenobiotic biotransformation.

the effects of 1- and 2-NP on liver enzyme activities were isomer specific and that 2-NP induced the activities of GSH S-transferases and UDP-glucuronyl transferase while 1-NP was more effective in inducing GSH peroxidases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
1- and 2-NP are metabolized to reactive intermediates that are capable of inducing changes in the activities of hepatic enzymes.
short-term inhalation of 1-NP or 2-NP induces changes in the levels of liver enzymes.

1-NP is more toxic than 2-NP, as it is a better inducer of microsomal cytosolic GSH peroxidases and is less effective as a microsomal inducer of cytochrome P-450 than 2-Np. 2-NP is better than 1-NP in the induction of microsomal UDP-glucuronoyltransferases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
inhalation of 1-NP or 2-NP at a concentration of 100 ppm does not induce hepatic toxicity.
the two isomers of nitropropane have differential effects on the liver.
the effects of short-term inhalational exposure to 1- and 2-nitrpropane are isomer specific.
